source.title: An Interpretable Neuron Embedding for Static Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Wei Han; Yangqiming Wang; C. Böhm; Jun-Ming Shao

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method—semantic-vector additive relations—to report polysemy in neurons of a vision model.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly says target neurons in Figure 3 show polysemy. Figure 2's similar-neuron visualizations, the KL-divergence curve, and the knowledge-distillation accuracy results do not measure polysemanticity and are not rows. The cited NetDissect result is from other work and is not included.
record.test_reason: This is a neuron-embedding and knowledge-distillation method paper. Polysemy comes up only in one aside on Figure 3 ('some neurons show polysemy'). That aside rests on additive semantic-vector visualizations. No polysemanticity measure, rate or set of unrelated input categories is reported, so the results show the method's behaviour rather than whether V1 holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that semantic vectors describe neuron semantics well, shown by qualitative visualizations and a falling KL divergence to NetDissect IoU targets. They also find that static knowledge distillation matches or beats relation-based distillation methods on CIFAR-100. The polysemy remark is a passing aside attributed to the lack of interpretability constraints in the pretrained model, not a conclusion of the paper.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses semantic-vector alignment and additive vector relations, rather than reproducing the original neuron-visualization or SoLU methods.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet18, semantic vectors of some 'complex' target neurons are approximated by pairwise sums of two simpler neurons' semantic vectors (Fig. 3; qualitative only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A neuron's semantics in a vision CNN can be decomposed into an additive combination of other neurons' semantics within the same layer.

record.problems: The polysemy evidence is qualitative and figure-based; the text does not specify the unrelated input categories or report a quantitative polysemanticity measure. The relevant visualization is for a single pre-trained vision model.

untested.parts: Whether ResNet18 neurons respond to several unrelated inputs. The paper only asserts polysemy of the Figure 3 target neurons and does not name the input categories or quantify it.
All parts; no language models are studied.
All parts; architectures are compared only for distillation accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The only polysemy statement is one sentence: 'some neurons show polysemy, as shown by target neurons in Figure 3'. There is no metric, no count and no description of the inputs. The NetDissect finding cited in the introduction (one neuron can carry several meanings) is other authors' work and is correctly excluded. The reader's limits_scope label on V1 is dropped because the rows cannot show V1's effect.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report explicit responses to several unrelated input categories or examples comparable to cat faces and car fronts.
The study does not test transformer language models or token/context polysemanticity.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
The study does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity.
The study does not compare architectures, activation functions, or regularization for their effects on polysemanticity.
The study does not use improved tools to establish that canonical mixed-response neurons detect one shared feature.
The study does not compare activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for their effect on polysemanticity.

rows.measure: Qualitative additive relation between neuron semantic vectors, illustrated with images.
rows.note: The text says target neurons in Figure 3 show polysemy. The figure's image-level semantics are not described in the text, so this does not establish responses to explicitly unrelated input categories.
rows.check: The measure is additive similarity between semantic vectors, not a neuron's response to unrelated inputs. The figure-only value cannot show V1's effect. The dataset is stated: Section 3.1 says interpretability experiments use ResNet18 (ImageNet-pretrained) on Broden.
